did_you_know.text: Did you know? The verse contrasts the wicked person, who flees even when no one is pursuing him, with the righteous, who are compared to a young lion confident in its strength. Confidence is thus presented as the result of moral character, not merely external power.

Did you know? Proverbs 28 connects crime in a land with the multiplication of rulers, while a discerning and knowledgeable person is portrayed as someone through whom leadership endures and is prolonged. The verse therefore also addresses the moral stability of society.

Did you know? The verse distinguishes between those who forsake the law and praise the wicked, and those who keep the law and oppose them. Keeping the law is portrayed not only as a personal faith, but also as a public stance against evil.

Did you know? According to the verse, a poor person who walks in integrity is better than a rich person whose ways are perverse. What matters most is not wealth, but a person's honesty and moral integrity.

Did you know? Proverbs 28 presents listening to the law as important even for prayer: whoever turns away from hearing the law—even that person's prayer is described as detestable. The verse emphasizes the connection between moral conduct and worship of God.

Did you know? The verse does not stop at confessing sin: it promises mercy to the person who confesses his sins and abandons them. Repentance therefore includes both acknowledging one's actions and changing direction.

Did you know? The verse praises the person who is always cautious—that is, someone who takes care and examines his ways—and warns against hardening the heart. Caution is presented as protection from falling into trouble.

Did you know? Proverbs 28 contrasts the person who works the land and has plenty of bread with the person who pursues worthless things and ends up with poverty. The verse commends useful, sustained work and warns against chasing things of no value.

Did you know? A faithful person is described as receiving abundant blessings, while the one who hastens to become rich will not go unpunished. The verse favors faithfulness and perseverance over hurried enrichment.

Did you know? The verse connects giving to the poor with having no lack, and turning one's eyes away from the poor with receiving many curses. It presents one's treatment of the vulnerable as a moral test with social consequences.
